title: Global infrastructure in one screen
rememberThis: An AWS Region is a separate geographic partition — data does not leave unless you configure cross-Region replication.
Availability Zones are isolated data centers within a Region; production workloads span at least two AZs.
Edge locations cache content near users — they are not Regions and do not run your EC2 instances.
Local Zones and Wavelength extend compute closer to users or 5G devices for ultra-low latency.
Route 53 and CloudFront route global traffic; Region choice still drives compliance and primary latency.
bullets: Check service availability in your target Region before architecture sign-off — not every service exists everywhere.
AZ names (a, b, c) are logical labels; do not assume they map to the same physical building across Regions.
Regional Edge Caches reduce origin load between CloudFront PoPs and your S3 or Application Load Balancer.
Opt-in Regions require explicit enablement in the account before deployment.
Multi-Region active-active is expensive — most teams use multi-AZ in one Region plus DR in another.
